223: Right after the second show at Toyota we set off for two more exhibitions in Zákupy, where there was also a corporate event for employees. A smaller event, where Martin's sparring partner Mirek Brunclík was already waiting for us with a workshop. Martin fixed his bike, but Márty Kabeláč crashed on the concrete; after treatment he sat by the obstacles with an ice cream and kept his fingers crossed for us. The two shows with a competition for volunteers ran a bit long, and we got egged on to a tape jump of around 125–130 cm.
224: We're sorting out the photos, so for now just a few quick ones in the gallery.
225: Going wild at an IT conference
226: Last week Vlasta and our young club gun Tobík Dolák rode an exhibition for Alternativo at the beautiful Valeč chateau, where they held a small IT conference focused on security. And since you ride safely on a bike too and the gentlemen from the management are athletes, they chose us. Low ceilings, a slippery floor, and Tobík forgot his helmet. Not exactly the ideal combo for an exhibition. The helmet wasn't a disaster, because one of the bosses is his dad – so as punishment he just had to tidy up.
227: We also roped in a young intern and a few conference visitors, so everyone was happy and we got a few photos too.

237: Opening of the CUBE STORE Karlovy Vary
238: Our Trialshow.cz team, which includes a large number of the Bikeskills project instructors, is slowly starting to develop a partnership with CUBE, the largest bike manufacturer in Europe.
239: The first swallow of this partnership was Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček signing a contract to promote the brand, followed straight away by this year's first exhibition at the opening of the CUBE STORE Karlovy Vary, hosted by the exceptional Marek Eben.
240: A luxurious, stylish shop full of bikes is a rarity these days. Vlasta and Martin Šimůnek jumped over the ribbon meant to be cut (and almost cut it with a chain on one of the jumps), and did a short show on small obstacles.
241: Martin Šimůnek then saddled a small kids' bike and showed that it's no problem to ride on the back wheel or hop on the front wheel even on an 18" bike :)
242: Children's day at Ladronka and Cycling day in Březno
243: Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Martin Šimůnek enjoyed two shows at Ladronka and one longer exhibition at the local Cycling Day in Březno on a beautiful, almost summery Sunday.
244: At Ladronka the guys were joined by a group of parkour athletes, and together they put on a decent show for a chanting crowd.
245: The Cycling Day was at a more relaxed pace, with Vlasta's offspring getting involved and firing up the local kids, who tried out the smallest obstacles after the exhibition. In the end even the parents ended up on bikes :)
247: There's not much riding to be done now, so it's time to service and upgrade our machines. Hopefully our November sale will help you with that. If you're interested in more products, write to us and we'll gladly recommend, advise and prepare a tailor-made offer.
249: Over the weekend Šimon and Čihi rode for Vodárek Transport in the picturesque town of Hulín. The guys' opening act was Zdeněk Izer. The weather was lucky in the truest sense of the word. A spur of a massive storm cloud ended exactly at Hulín, and if the guys had turned left instead of right at the junction, they would have driven straight into rain instead of a beautiful sunny day. We rode a slightly longer and more action-packed version of the exhibition, the spectators were great and we're glad for the praise from the organisers. Hopefully back in Hulín soon.
251: The second day camp started with a rainy day and temperatures below 20°C. Surprisingly, that didn't put off many participants, and combined with the growing interest in our camps, 27 kids came along plus a few from our club. We originally didn't want to exceed the rider limit we'd set, but the kids were disciplined and loved the bikes, so our main carers and coaches could handle it. Unfortunately we had to turn away further substitutes – hopefully see you next year.
252: We covered everything from the pump track, berms and obstacles to jumps for the bravest. On Thursday there was also Trial training for everyone who owns a Trial bike. Those who don't still had the chance to try the basics during one of the sessions. The final pump track race was dramatic until the end and a nice full stop to the whole camp, where you could see improvement in most riders. Every day there were also rides around the area to build fitness (although that's not our priority, unlike technique).
253: Women Tune Up with BIKESKILLS vol. 2
254: We have another one-day camp for women and girls behind us, created at the request of our clients and friends, and also thanks to interest from participants of the first camp.
255: As interest in the camp was a bit greater than last time, we called to arms not only Katarína, Mára and Vlasta, but also Lukáš Valný, who was missing last time, and special thanks for rescuing the tent and looking after our things go to Matouš Balík from our home club.
256: The morning programme was devoted to basic technique – in other words, we learn what we'll try to use off-road in the afternoon. At noon we rode at an easy pace to Hotel Legner Zvánovice, where all participants refuelled, and after a short break we practised off-road riding.
257: There was also a workshop by Mára Tryner focused on classic bike maintenance and dealing with emergency situations riders may encounter on the bike.
258: Thanks to all participants and instructors – hopefully we'll soon manage to put together next year's calendar with events for everyone.
259: Exhibitions and workshops in Bartošovice, Vrbátky and Malé Žernoseky
260: Triple exhibitions are always more demanding, both in coordinating times and the team. If workshops are added, it's even more demanding. Martin Šimůnek, Michal Budský and Mára Tryner set off on a longer route to Bartošovice and Vrbátky, where crowds of spectators and bike enthusiasts awaited them.
261: The guys showed what they could and at the same time taught those interested Trial and MTB in our workshops. Vlasta, Lukáš Valný and Tobík Dolák went the opposite way to Malé Žernoseky, where besides the exhibition their task was a mini workshop for visitors.
262: After swapping slots with the dog handlers (so the dogs could have some peace), we rode the show, tested the local concrete walls a bit and held a mini workshop. Thanks for the invitation and the great turnout.
264: The crisis has been here for a few weeks now and caught us in the middle of preparing our project. Being flexible, instead of sitting on our hands we decided to film a few coaching lessons for the boys and girls from our club {1}MTB & TRIAL Mraveniště Říčany{2} . The first piece is more of an attempt to produce something that makes sense without a camera, a microphone or any directing experience.
265: For now we're going for less information and more watching, so we'll see what feedback we get from our training group.
267: The date of the event was set last spring, but it was still unclear whether the event could be held this year at all. We knew we were going for a lean solution and adapted the programme accordingly. One of the big concessions was cancelling the riders from England, as it was impossible to predict how the pandemic and the limits on the number of starters would develop.{1}In the end we kept the event in the Tehov park again, thanks also to the support of the municipality and local people, and it turned out to be a good choice. The preparation itself was marked by rain and storms, which complicated mainly the pump track and in the end forced us to cancel the beam and log section for Trial, which we shed a few tears over given all the fine-tuning.
268: {1}We won't beat around the bush. The weather turned out great, over 90 riders came, and thanks to TERRA (JCB), Autosalon BENO Říčany (ŠKODA), the Inplem farm, the Tehov volunteer fire brigade, instructor Klárka Hájková, the guys from Cage Warriors, perfect sound and hosting by Aleš Matoušek and many volunteers, an estimated 500–600 spectators came throughout the day. In the morning they cheered on the Trial riders and the motorbike exhibition by Dalibor Šulc and Tomáš Hůla. Some combined it with a trip from the children's day in Říčany, so the chance to operate a digger, pet the cows or play with the firefighters' equipment was certainly an interesting bonus for all the kids (and, let's be honest, for us parents and riders too).{2}This year Trial was divided into several parts. Unfortunately holidays and injuries weakened our club line-up a bit, and some took on organisational duties rather than the handlebars, but even so the kids' categories filled up beyond expectations. After the kids, the Elite riders took to the course. As it was an exhibition race, everyone rode in one category, so the guys could compare themselves with each other as in the final of a big race. The courses were rideable and set with the weather in mind, but there were a few sharper passages too. Lukáš Valný deserves huge respect – despite being heavily involved in the organisation, he finished third. Matouš Balík's performance was a surprise: although he's a junior by age, thanks to consistent riding he scored just 6 penalty points. The club kids were curious about Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček's performance, and probably even he didn't know what to expect after 2 years without racing, with 40 on his neck and after his 6th knee operation. A new bike and a relaxed race resulted in 0 penalty points, so there was no contest.
269: {1}The break between the kids' and adults' practice was filled with a small jumping contest, won once again with an exhibition performance by Vlasta, with 120 cm over the tape and a 225 cm jump off a height, ahead of Lukáš Valný, Tomáš Kočička and Matouš Balík.
270: {1}In the afternoon the main roles were played by the boys and girls on the pump track, battling against the clock at a very sharp pace. Lots of kids came to see how much they could get out of themselves. The highlight of the day was the full-suspension race, dominated by the local duo of Lukáš's. Lukáš Turek took first place and also fifth in Experts (hardtails). After the Trial and especially the whole week of preparations, Lukáš Valný had to wake up a bit, but made up for it with 2nd place, becoming the only rider to stand on the podium in all disciplines.
271: {1}The junior category was taken by talented rider Tobík Dolák, who after a very decent Trial performance jumped on a hardtail and won ahead of the winner of one of the kids' Trial categories, Jonáš Vavřinec, and Tommi Neuwirth.{2}The highlight of the event was the Expert category race, with a number of top riders including MTB legend Michal Maroši. Michal suffered a bit after his vaccination, but switched into race mode, grabbed the prize money with first place, including the best jump award, ahead of Alex Sidor and Hugo Novák. Unfortunately there was no shortage of crashes either. The Best Crash award went to Martin Králíček, who luckily only came away with a decent supply of scrapes. Worse was the result of an innocent misstep by Martin Vavřinec, who chose the pump track race over Trial and unfortunately tore his cruciate ligament. We wish him a speedy recovery. The best-placed woman, despite a dislocating shoulder and three kids to look after, was another instructor from the club – Katarína Tóthová.
272: {1}Many thanks to everyone for taking part, helping and supporting. We are donating part of the entry fees to support people affected by the tornado. Unfortunately this also affected several riders who were supposed to come, so hopefully it will help a little. We also thank the municipality of Tehov for supporting the event and lending us the park, and of course the town of Říčany.
273: {1}A video from the event will follow – hopefully see you at the next edition. You can also watch a short report on ČT Déčko (we'll announce the date).
274: {1}The team of the MTB & TRIAL Mraveniště Říčany club and the organisers of Říčanské Šlapačky
276: We held the first two classic camps of our Bikeskills project, once again split into female bikers (Saturday) and male bikers (Sunday). Surprisingly, once again more women came, and thanks to the weather too it turned into a relaxed day on the bike, where the women made progress on everything we came across, including steps, benches and things they probably wouldn't ride on their own. There were fewer men, and all the more exhausted they were. Fewer riders, more riding :) All under the guidance of Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Katarína Tóthová. We hope the riders found a new perspective on riding and perhaps goals for the future.
